Within about a 5 minutes drive from there, is the Ramboda Waterfall where a hotel is located. If you walk to the bottom floor you can access the trail which leads to the Waterfall itself and have lunch at the restaurant afterwards.

Peaceful walk for about 45 minutes down and backDefinitely worth visiting Enjoy

body: If you visit Sri Lanka this should be place to visit.Devon Falls is situated in Talawakele, Nuwara Eliya District. The falls is named after a pioneer English coffee planter called Devon, whose plantation is situated nearby the falls. The Waterfall is 97 metres high. Plan on visiting Devon's and St Clair waterfall on the same day as they are situated in the same area.You can expect cooler climate in this area so be ready with rain jackets/umbrella or a spring jacket. Right in front of the place where you park the vehicle you will find a restaurant with delicious Ceylon tea, cakes and rolls (spicy but great).

body: Travelling from Nuwara Eliya to Colombo on A7 we came across this beautiful waterfall that plunges down to the valley below in three continuous cascades. The waterfall is the 19th tallest waterfall in Sri Lanka and it is 97 meters high. The best place to view the waterfall is the clearly marked area by the side of the main road.A closer look can be had from the nearby Melsna tea Castle while sipping a cup of delicious Ceylon Tea. Not very far from Devon is the widest water fall in Sri lanka St. Clairs fall.
title: 19th Tallest Waterfall

title: It's a waterfall
body: Devon Falls is a waterfall and viewing point on the A7 out of Nuwara Eliya towards Hatton. The road was being widened when we travelled it and was in quite unbelievably bad condition, with roadworks stretching some 20km and parts of the road no more than a muddy, rutted track.Somewhat disconcertingly, behind you as you look out at the waterfall there is a Victorian tea room - this is actually the Devon Tea Centre, which we didn't visit. Just along the road is the Mlesna Tea Castle, a very strange building which we also passed by.Other than that, it's a waterfall. A very nice waterfall, but a waterfall for all that...
